It's wonderful to see some truths being told to counteract all the prevarications often shared in regular media sources.

I won't argue with that. Have you heard this theory about Snowden being a "limited hangout"? I've not really looked into it at all but I've heard it mentioned once or twice.

Posting Wikipedia definition for "Limited Hangout" for clarity as I'd no doubt make a balls of trying to explain;

A limited hangout, or partial hangout, is a public relations or propaganda technique that involves the release of previously hidden information in order to prevent a greater exposure of more important details.

It could well be paranoid delusion but food for thought in any case.

It's an interesting concept to be sure, and I agree that a certain amount of paranoia is healthy nowadays. The explanation I heard given was that there is literally so much information that it it were dumped all at once, so much signal would go unnoticed amongst all the noise. In other words, minor scandals (that still deserve our attention) would be swamped by major scandals and would end up ignored.

Yeah I can understand that and if that's the way it's really going down then fair play to Snowden. I'd like to think that I'd show as much resolve against such a terrifying entity as the U.S. Government (and their Military/Intelligence network) but I guess you don't really know until you're in that situation. It does strike me as bizarre though that whistleblowers are largely vilified in the U.S. when clearly they are working in the interests of the people en masse rather than the demonstrably shady organisations that seek to fool the populace. I can totally understand the NSA (or whoever happens to be implicated) being royally pissed off and, by extension, the federal governments desire to make examples of whistleblowers. What I don't get is why the people consider the likes of Snowden and Manning traitors.
I guess for most people it's just easier to believe what you are told rather than sift through the facts and make up your own mind.

It's horse shit propagated by those who seek to discredit Snowden. Citizenfour itself is a fantastic rebuttal to that. The unending chorus of "limited hangout" in regards to Snowden on /r/conspiracy alone should tell you something is amiss.

If you are knowledgeable and think critically there is no reason to believe Snowden is anything but on the level. The "criticism" that he didn't reveal 9/11 or something is ridiculous - he's clear about his area of knowledge and access and has dropped megaton fucking bombs all over that area. Ask your most technically skilled friends about what has come out of those documents and they will agree that it is serious fucking shit.

I do however entertain that Pierre Omidyar's First Look media venture is absolutely an attempt at containment. The descriptions of how Taibbi's venture went off are very telling and Omidyar has some very sketchy intelligence connections.

Yes I hopped over to Reddit earlier for the Snowden AMA and I am now convinced that he is the real deal, not that I had any overwhelming doubts in the first place. Very inspiring and he gave the impression of being quite down to earth to boot. If you haven't read it I would definitely recommend taking a look.
